Optimism among American firms in China has reached a record low as
the impact of ongoing COVID-related restrictions is negatively impacting business confidence
and leading to lower investment.
According to a survey from the American Chamber of Commerce in Shanghai,
released on Friday, October 28,
the number of companies describing themselves as optimistic about the five-year business outlook
dropped to 55%.
The figure reached the lowest level in the survey's history, down 23% from 2021.
In addition, 52% of the companies said that their headquarters' business confidence in China's
economic management deteriorated in the past year.
Only 18% of them ranked China as top place in their country's global investment plans,
down from 27% in 2021.
The survey noted,
one-third of respondents have redirected planned China investments to other destinations in the past year,
almost double the number of companies that did so in 2021.
In terms of earning performance, the outlook for the China market is dim for American firms,
as nearly half of the companies forecast their yearly revenue growth in 2022,
down 29% from 2021, and the lowest expectation in at least 10 years,
and 75% of companies reported profits in 2021, significantly below rates from the past several years.
Companies in the survey considered domestic competition their top challenge for the next five years in China.
Other factors include the U.S.-China tensions, economic slowdown, and COVID restrictions.
Sean Stein, chairman of China's AmCham, said,
What keeps a lot of businesses up at night is competition and rising competition from Chinese competitors.
Beijing's strict COVID measures remain the main concern for domestic and foreign companies in China.
During last week's CCP National Congress, Chinese leader Xi Jinping showed no signs of easing policy,
prompting a global sell-off in Chinese stocks.
Affected by the zero-COVID policy, many Chinese companies have been facing no orders from outside and no domestic consumption.
They have been forced to lay off employees.
One of the latest victims is Chinese big data solutions provider Mininglamp Technology,
an artificial intelligence unicorn company in China.
According to Time News, Mininglamp Technology has recently disclosed that more than 70% of the company's employees have been fired.
The workforce is now left with more than 1,000 people.
At its peak, the company had between 5,000 and 6,000 employees.
Mininglamp Technology has once been the most valued big data company in China.
Founded in 2014, Mininglamp Technology secured 1.2 billion yuan,
166 million dollars in its first three rounds of funding.
By 2018, it had a valuation of over 1 billion dollars,
making it a unicorn in the artificial intelligence sector.
According to Yitzai Global,
The company has partnered with many industry leaders such as Tencent on urban digitalization, marketing, and government affairs.
But under the zero-COVID policy, many other Chinese companies, including Mininglamp,
cannot receive foreign or domestic orders.
They must adopt austerity policies and downsize office space or layoff workers.
Mininglamp Technology has reported multiple layoffs for more than a year, firing employees across the board in many departments.
According to the company's employees, the big data star has disbanded its R&D department
and laid off workers in the digital city and financial departments.
The company is still struggling to manage legal severance payments for laid-off employees.
According to financial experts, large-scale layoffs in Mininglamp Technology are very rare in the unicorn company.
As a high-tech field on which the Chinese government depends,
the company's development prospects are supposed to be promising.
However, the layoffs show that even a unicorn company is beginning to lose its edge.
Mininglamp Technology is a representative of the AI industry, and its layoffs are not at all a problem for one company.
It can be seen that China's entire AI big data industry is in crisis,
and this is an indicator of a full-blown recession and the loss of vitality in an economy.
China's Ministry of National Defense held its monthly press conference on October 27, 2022.
The meeting occurred after the Chinese Communist Party, or CCP, finished holding its 20th Congress.
The press conference showed that U.S.-China relations would continue to freeze after the CCP Congress.
Beijing believes it has not made any mistakes in its relationship with the U.S.
According to CNA, when asked about U.S. Defense Secretary Austin's desire to reopen the military
communication channel between the two countries, Chinese Defense Ministry spokesman Tan Kefei said the
current contentious relationship between the two sides is serious and the responsibility rests
entirely with the U.S.
Tan Kefei blamed the U.S. for blurring and hollowing out the one-China principle, repeatedly instigating arms sales
to Taiwan, and creating obstacles to China's peaceful reunification.
U.S. officials have repeatedly stated that under the Taiwan Relations Act, the U.S. government is responsible for
providing appropriate defensive weapons depending on the military threat that Taiwan faces.
U.S.-China relations have become more strained following House Speaker Nancy Pelosi's historic visit to Taiwan in August.
Pelosi's visit came amid concerns that the CCP will launch a war of aggression against Taiwan, similar to what Moscow did with Ukraine,
after Xi won an absolute victory at the CCP 20th Congress to stay in office.
There were many predictions that Beijing might increase tensions in the Taiwan Strait, even soon invading the island.
President Biden has stated that the U.S. will defend Taiwan if the island is invaded.
According to surveys, most Taiwanese do not want to reunify with China when the CCP still dominates the country.
Specifically, most Taiwanese reject living under the one-country-two-systems policy that the CCP has applied in Hong Kong,
and is trying to convince Taiwan to accept.
And speaking of enemies of America's society and America's future, China has managed to completely
hollow out our American institutions at every level. They have captured America, so to speak.
From everything to intellectual property theft, to using apps like TikTok to destroy our culture and college
campuses, to brainwash kids into anti-American ideals. Now, my next guest has an op-ed out for this titled,
Elite Capture What It Is and How It Threatens America's Future. In it, Scott Powell, the author writes,
quote, while the CCP uses front groups for propaganda, they have mastered all manner of techniques with an
emphasis on infiltration to influence, compromise and co-op elites so as to, quote, capture them.
typical targets include university professors and scientists, media executives and reporters,
and political and corporate leaders. He joins me right now, the author of that piece, author and senior
fellow at the Discovery Institute, Scott Powell. Scott, it's great to have you on the show. I really enjoyed
this op-ed. Breakdown for our audience, what is the elite capture that you speak of in this piece?
Scott Powell Well, it's nice to be with you, Addison. Elite capture is a process, a technique and a process,
and I must add that it is generally a form of corruption to start with. Understand that elite capture
generally involves corruption. One elite or one party to come to influence, sometimes subliminally,
indirectly, indirectly, over time, so as to ultimately get that other party to do the bidding of the
controlling party. So elite capture means taking control of other people or institutions. It could
be labor unions. It could be a whole host of things, and we can talk about some of those. But coming to
influence them in such a way for a political purpose, it's almost always for a political purpose.
Scott Powell Well, and it really is unbelievable, we'll say, how well China has infiltrated
American society from corporations like the NBA and like Nike to running applications with Apple like
TikTok that are just, you know, in my opinion, they're using TikTok as this tool to just destroy
Western civilization, Western culture by boosting, you know, all of these sorts of influencers,
these leftist influencers, right? And using TikTok potentially as a security breach to track people's
data, gather information on them. China has done a really impressive job. And yet so many of our elected
officials, this is out in the open. They obviously will profit off of the death of Western civilization.
So many leaders in America today, Scott, don't seem to do anything about this. In fact, so many of them
are bought and owned by the CCP. What are we supposed to do about that?
Scott Powell Well, this is a starting point, Addison. You're educating them. Let's hope
that this program gets widely watched because a lot of people don't even understand this phenomenon at
all. It happens psychologically, subliminally. And you know, the communists are making war against us
through propaganda, ideology and propaganda, through psychological operations, we call them psyops,
and then also infiltration. And elite capture really involves all of them, but a big emphasis on
infiltrating society. And that's done oftentimes behind the scenes with people not knowing what's really
happening. For instance, the Chinese have a sister city program that has built relationships with cities
across the United States that have a sister relationship with a Chinese city. And oftentimes, these programs
over time, create goodwill. And then when the Chinese want to come in and carry out a business transaction,
like a land purchase, China now owns a lot of land in the United States. They were so successful in North
Dakota with their elite capture that they captured one of their universities, Dickinson State University.
There was a big scandal there about 12 years ago involving the Chinese. They sort of brushed it under the
carpet. Well, the Chinese observe all these things and they could see that we really don't take a stand.
And so they've conducted another operation where they've acquired land near the Grand Forks Air Force Base,
which is also a space force base with the most sophisticated technology in America, all done with elite capture.
Yeah, they're local people in Grand Forks.
They're famously buying up land in the US and around Canada, I believe. And they're doing this near all of
our military bases across the world. And a lot of people, they don't hear about this because CNN, MSNBC,
they don't cover it. Also, the DOJ just charged over 13 Chinese nationals with various crimes for potential
interference in American politics, potential influence in national security threats.
And people don't hear about this. They're not going to hear about that from Rachel Maddow, from
Don Lemon and from all these hacks in the mainstream media, because they are on the side of China,
all the way up to and including Joe Biden. And you write this in your piece, without a doubt,
the greatest elite captured by the CCP has been the Joe Biden family, which started at least as far back
as 2013. So not only is America writ large being attacked from within by China, we are,
China has essentially bought the president of the United States, Scott.
Robert R. 20 years ago, if you had said that one day the Chinese would own the Oval Office,
would control the Oval Office, that would have been preposterous. But it has happened. And it's
happened right in front of us. I think another good example of elite capture is what the World Economic
Forum does. You know, the World Economic Forum believes that national sovereignty should be
suspended and that we should go to a new global order where people would own nothing. And they've
actually gotten many elites to buy into this or at least participate in their programs in Davos. You
have, you know, French President Emmanuel Macron going. You have, you know, I mean,
Klaus Schwab is taking great pride in capturing the cabinet of Prime Minister Justin Trudeau in our
Canadian, in our neighbor to the north, Canada.
Yeah.
And the list goes on. There's the New Zealand Prime Minister. There are government officials from Argentina
and Australia, all that have participated in WEF. And we find that most of these countries have moved
left during these years. So we can no longer even maybe count on them as being an ally in the Pacific.
In the case of Australia, we just don't know.
So I know.
I know.
